job.style: a market or shop situation that uses the idea

passage: Rohan visits a local electronics market to buy components for his science project. He needs two types of resistors. The first type is sold in packs of 3^2, which the shopkeeper explains means 3 multiplied by itself, resulting in 9 resistors. Rohan also considers a special high-precision resistor priced at 2^(-3) rupees. The shopkeeper clarifies that a negative exponent indicates a reciprocal, so the price is 1 divided by 2 cubed, or 1/8 of a rupee. Next, Rohan looks at a micro-chip that measures 0.0007 meters in length. The shopkeeper explains that to write this in standard form, we move the decimal point four places to the right to get 7, so it is written as 7 x 10^(-4). Finally, Rohan compares two capacitors. One has a capacity of 3 x 10^4 microfarads and the other has 2 x 10^5 microfarads. The shopkeeper warns him not to add the coefficients and exponents together, as 3 x 10^4 plus 2 x 10^5 is not 5 x 10^9, but rather 230,000 microfarads. Rohan learns that exponents follow strict rules to ensure calculations remain accurate for his project.
